newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LIGHTNING BEAT BLUES TO RUN UNBEATEN STREAK TO SIX.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LIGHTNING BEAT BLUES TO RUN UNBEATEN STREAK TO SIX.

text.p: Daymond Langkow and Dino Ciccarelli continued their torrid scoring and Rick Tabaracci turned aside 33 shots Tuesday as the Tampa Bay Lightning ran their unbeaten streak to six games with a 3-2 defeat of the St Louis Blues.
Tampa Bay is 5-0-1 during its unbeaten stretch, which is one short of the club record set late last season.
Mikael Andersson and Langkow, who has 11 points in his last seven games, staked the Lightning to a 2-0 advantage 110 seconds into the contest.

Ciccarelli's 25th goal came on the power play with 2:31 left in the second period and gave Tampa Bay a 3-1 advantage. Ciccarelli has points in his last eight games with six goals and four assists during that span.

Brett Hull continued his torrid scoring pace for the Blues, who lost for just the second time in their last 12 road games. Hull, who had his 36th and 37th goals, has scored in 20 of his last 23 games (19-13-32).

Hull drew the Blues within a goal in the first period and the game remained tight into the second period. The Blues had a chance to tie the game midway through the session when Hull broke in alone on Tabaracci but the Tampa Bay goalie denied the breakaway attempt.

St. Louis had an even better chance with five minutes remaining when Hull took advantage of a 2-on-1 breakaway. Hull gathered in the rebound of the initial shot attempt and had an open net but Tabaracci turned aside his chance by scrambling on his stomach to deflect the puck away.
"You try to stay with the puck as long as you can," Tabaracci said. "It was a fortunate save, not great or lucky -- just fortunate. It was my second effort that allowed me to stop it."
"Earlier in the season we lost some games we should have won," Lightning coach Terry Crisp said. "Tonight we could have lost if Tabaracci didn't play out of his skull."
Hull scored just 20 seconds into the third period but the Blues were unable to get any more good scoring chances.
"Tampa started fast and we didn't do anything to counteract it," Hull said. "We just have to get better in the beginning."

At Los Angeles, Ed Olczyk set up the go-ahead tally and scored a late insurance goal and Stephane Fiset made 32 saves as the Kings snapped Colorado's winning streak at six games with a 3-1 triumph over the Avalanche.
Roman Vopat scored the deciding goal just 11 seconds after Stephane Yelle tied the game for Colorado seven minutes into the second period. Vladimir Tsyplakov scored the Kings' first goal.
Los Angeles has won three straight for the third time this season and became just the third team to beat the defending champions twice this year, joining the Blues and Flames.
Fiset has allowed just six goals in his last five games.
In Vancouver, Mark Recchi had two goals and an assist and Jocelyn Thibault made 28 saves as the Montreal Canadians solidified their playoff standing with a 4-2 victory over the Canucks.
Vladimir Malakhov and Jassen Cullimore each had a goal for the Canadiens, who lead Hartford for the seventh playoff berth in the Eastern Conference by one point.
Alexander Mogilny and Martin Gelinas scored for Vancouver, which has lost three straight, falling one point behind the Calgary Flames for the eighth and final playoff spot in the Western Conference.

In Chicago, Arturs Irbe got his second shutout in five games and 10th of his career and Todd Harvey took advantage of a slip by defenceman Keith Carney to score the only goal of the game as the Dallas Stars edged the Blackhawks 1-0.
Irbe stopped 24 shots, including 12 in the third period. He saved his best stop for last, stonewalling Chicago's top goal scorer Tony Amonte from in tight with 95 seconds remaining.
At Florida, David Nemirovsky scored 94 seconds into the third period to lift the Panthers to a 2-2 tie against the San Jose Sharks.
Nemirovsky was at the left doorstep when he re-directed Dave Lowry's pass past goaltender Kelly Hrudey for his fourth goal.

The Panthers extended their unbeaten streak to six games (0-4-2) and tied the Sharks for the second time this season. Florida had a chance to win the game but Hrudey made a diving kick save on a shot by Rob Niedermayer from the slot with just under four minutes left in the extra session.
Hrudey made 31 saves for the Sharks, who have just one win in their last nine games (1-6-2). San Jose outshot Florida 40-33.
